questions.question: How large is the client company?
questions.why: Size shapes how much change the organization can absorb and what kind of team it needs.

questions.question: Are they an existing client of ours?
questions.why: An existing relationship changes how much trust and context we can draw on.

questions.question: What work, if any, have we done for them before?
questions.why: Past engagements tell us what they valued and what we already know about their environment.

questions.question: What budget range is realistic for this?
questions.why: Budget decides whether we propose a phased approach or a full program.

questions.question: What is the timetable, and are there any hard deadlines?
questions.why: A fixed deadline often matters more to the approach than the budget does.

questions.question: Who is the decision maker, and who else needs to be on board?
questions.why: The right solution has to be one the people who decide will actually back.

questions.question: What would success look like to the client a year from now?
questions.why: A clear picture of success keeps the solution aimed at the outcome rather than the activity.
